decision: CORS echoes the exact request Origin and is gated by the same rule as admission; --allow-origin and allowedOrigins take a hostname (any scheme and port, as before) or an origin such as https://app.example.com (exact scheme, host and port)
why: the page on an allowed origin holds the user's API key, and a hostname entry trusts every port and scheme on that host, so operators need a way to name one origin; hostnames keep working so no existing flag breaks; one predicate for admission and the echo, so a request is never admitted yet unreadable; an entry with a path, uppercase or a trailing slash throws at creation and is rejected by the CLI instead of silently never matching

decision: preflight answers 204 with Allow-Methods POST and Allow-Headers Content-Type, Accept, MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method, Mcp-Name, X-Redmine-API-Key, Max-Age 7200, Vary Origin; no Allow-Credentials; no Expose-Headers; Mcp-Session-Id, Last-Event-ID and Authorization left out
why: the endpoint serves POST only (GET, DELETE and OPTIONS answer 405 as the handler is stateless); the 2026-07-28 spec drops Mcp-Session-Id and Last-Event-ID, the handler issues no session id, and it reads no Authorization header; the SDK client reads only mcp-session-id, www-authenticate and dpop-nonce from responses and the handler sends none, so there is nothing to expose; Chrome caps preflight caching at 2 hours
evidence: probe of the handler: GET, DELETE, OPTIONS and PUT answer 405 with only content-type, POST answers SSE with cache-control, connection, content-type, x-accel-buffering; spec 2026-07-28 transport page via ctx7

decision: a preflight is an OPTIONS with Origin and Access-Control-Request-Method; Host then Origin are checked first, so a rebound Host or a foreign Origin gets the unchanged 403 with no CORS headers; other OPTIONS fall through to the endpoint
why: keeps the DNS rebinding defence ahead of everything else and avoids answering a plain OPTIONS from a non-browser as a preflight
evidence: unit tests: preflight refused for foreign Origin and for Host evil.example:3737, plain OPTIONS answers 401 without CORS headers
